topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s aims and introduces the hallmark framework that will organize its explanations of cancer.

topics.label: Mutations that deregulate growth and survival signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways allow cancer cells to proliferate and survive without normal growth control.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted cell maturation contributes to cancer by comparing differentiation in blood-cell lineages and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of the p53-regulated balance between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic proteins prevents cancer cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell division and how increased telomerase expression allows cancer cells to bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consolidate how cellular safeguards constrain cancer growth and how genetic mutations undermine those safeguards.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the molecular changes driving it.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit a vascular supply to overcome the limits imposed by oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and successful secondary growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what enables cancer cells to spread from a primary tumor and establish detectable tumors at distant sites.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by restating its central message and learning expectations before offering further reading and inviting questions.
